# The chat gateway and the Harness hosts it starts, in one image.
#
# Two runtimes, each for its own job: Bun runs the gateway (`gateway/server.ts`)
# and installs the dependencies from `bun.lock`; Node runs each person's
# Harness host, because DeepSeek Harness requires Node 22.19 or later. Bun is
# copied in from its own image at the version the lockfile was written with,
# rather than installed by a script fetched at build time.
FROM oven/bun:1.3.14-debian AS bun

FROM node:22-bookworm-slim
COPY --from=bun /usr/local/bin/bun /usr/local/bin/bun

WORKDIR /chat

# Manifests first, so a source change does not reinstall. The two plugins are
# workspace packages and the install needs their manifests to link them.
COPY package.json bun.lock bunfig.toml ./
COPY plugins/business-tools/package.json plugins/business-tools/
COPY plugins/business-nodes/package.json plugins/business-nodes/
# Harness's own install scripts stay blocked, as in development: the lockfile
# is the dependency set, and nothing fetched at install time joins it.
RUN bun install --frozen-lockfile --production

COPY gateway gateway
COPY plugins plugins
COPY profile profile
COPY skills skills
COPY AGENTS.md tsconfig.json ./

# Host homes, session logs and documents. Mount a volume here: a person's
# conversations live in it.
ENV CHAT_DATA_DIR=/chat/.data
RUN mkdir -p /chat/.data && chown -R node:node /chat/.data
USER node

EXPOSE 3100
CMD ["bun", "gateway/server.ts"]
/chat-deepseek/README.md:
# The business chat

Every application this generator writes ships with this chat, in its `chat/`
directory. A person signs in once, with their account in the application, and
from then on works in plain language. The chat finds records, runs the
business's reports, and opens the application's **own screens inside the
conversation**, where the person creates, edits and approves. The same sign-in
reaches the reporting platform, whose reports open in the conversation too.

It is a [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deepseek-ai/dsh)
composition, pinned to **0.2.0-rc.2** exactly. A gateway in front of it owns
everything Harness should not: who the person is, what they may reach, and
the credentials that reach it.

```
browser ─► nginx ─► /chat/ ─► gateway (Bun)  ──────────► one Harness host per person
                │               Better Auth sessions        127.0.0.1 only, its own home,
                │               single sign-on broker       the business composition:
                │               view ids, refs               four reads, four screen openers,
                │               host manager, proxy          the skills — nothing else
                │                     ▲                            │ tool calls
                │                     └────────────────────────────┘
                │               tools run here, as the person, against:
                ├─► /        the application (Loco backend + TanStack Start, ?embed=1 in a card)
                └─► /report  the reporting platform (embed routes, assertion sign-in)
```

## What the person can do

| Ask | What happens |
|---|---|
| "Find the open opportunities for Acme" | `search_records`, as the person, through the application's own three access gates |
| "What state is that deal in?" | `get_record_summary`: fields, status, whether the status is final, the moves allowed from it |
| "Open it" / "I want to change the amount" | `open_record` / `open_update_form`: the application's screen, in a card |
| "Create a new support case" | `open_create_form`: the application's empty form, in a card |
| "Approve it" | `request_approval`: the record at its lifecycle bar with that move preselected; the person presses it |
| "Which accounts grew most this quarter?" | `search_reports`, then `run_approved_report`: a paged table, a chart where the report defines one |

**The model never writes a record.** It has no tool that writes. A save
happens in the embedded screen, under the application's validation, rules,
permissions and optimistic locking. If someone else saved first, the screen
shows the conflict dialog: refresh to their version, or overwrite. The save
reaches the conversation as an `[Application]` event only after the gateway has
read the record back. Until then the assistant may say the form is open, and
not that anything was saved.

## Sign-in: the chat is the broker, both applications keep their own

1. The person signs in at `/chat/_/sign-in` with their **application**
   account. The gateway checks it against the application's
   `POST /api/auth/login`, opens its own Better Auth session
   (`chat.session_token`), and relays the application's session cookie, so the
   embedded screens are signed in. Sign-in is rate-limited per client address.
2. For the reporting platform, the gateway signs a **60-second Ed25519
   assertion** with `SSO_SIGNING_KEY`: `iss`, `aud: "report"`, the person's
   email and roles, a single-use `jti`. The platform's
   `POST /api/auth/assertion` verifies it against `SSO_PUBLIC_KEY`. It refuses
   any lifetime over 120 seconds, any replayed `jti`, and any deactivated
   account. It then opens the platform's own session, matching the person's
   roles by name to the reporting roles the pack created from the same
   `rbac`, and re-syncs them on every sign-in.
3. Signing out of the chat ends all three sessions.

**The model never sees** a token, a cookie, a raw URL, an id or SQL. Records
reach it as opaque `ref`s issued to that person. A screen is a **view id**:
it lasts `CHAT_VIEW_TTL_SECONDS` (600 by default), and is checked against
its owner and re-authorised with the application every time it is opened. A
card whose view has expired offers **Re-open**, which mints a new one after
the same checks.

## The composition

`profile/business.patch.yml` is applied to every host as the last `--patch`
layer, so nothing on disk can widen it. It disables every row that leaves the
business surface:

- shells and subprocesses;
- the sandbox and terminals;
- workspace files and uploads;
- web fetch and search;
- MCP;
- programmatic tool calling;
- sub-agents and workflows;
- the plugin manager;
- other model providers;
- telemetry.

It inserts one agent preset, `business`, whose tools are this package's eight
and `skill`. `bun run test:composition` composes the patch over the shipped
bundles and **fails on any enabled package outside `ALLOWED_PACKAGES`**. It
then boots a host and checks the agent's tool catalog.

The gateway proxies a host's HTTP and WebSocket surface to its owner only, and
filters it by endpoint, not merely by route. Harness's mux socket can open any
endpoint, so every `open` frame goes through the same allowlist
(`checkMuxFrame`). `settings` is read-only (`describe`), because a settings
write could repoint the DeepSeek base URL that the server's key is sent to.

## Skills

`skills/` holds nine skills on working *in* an application:

- using it;
- finding, creating and updating records, and conflicts;
- workflows and approvals;
- reports;
- charts and dashboards;
- roles and access;
- asking questions in plain language.

The generator adds a tenth for each project, `skills/<project>-domain/SKILL.md`.
It is written from the compiled model, so the assistant's vocabulary is the
application's own: every record type with its help text, its fields and its
line items; every value list and what each value means; every lifecycle,
listing its moves, its final states and who may make each move; the roles and
what each may read; and the reports the business asked for. `AGENTS.md` holds
the operating rules, which no skill overrides.

## Memory: what one person costs, measured

There is no model on the server: DeepSeek runs the model, so memory here is
processes, and **the term that scales is one Harness host per signed-in
person.** `bun run load` (`tests/load/host-memory.ts`) measures it. It signs
real accounts in through the real gateway, which starts each person's host,
and has each person ask questions. Each question makes a real
`search_records` call, through the gateway and the application, as that
person. The model is the one thing scripted: its words are canned, its tool
call is not. RSS and PSS are read from `/proc` per host process.

**PSS** divides each shared page among the processes sharing it. Summed over
hosts, it is what they take from the machine, and it is the figure to plan
capacity with. RSS counts shared pages in every process and overstates the
total.

Measured on 2026-10-04, on a 16 GB, 4-core Linux machine, CRM model, role
*Sales Rep*, `CHAT_HOST_HEAP_MB=256`:

| hosts | turns each | phase | per host PSS | per host RSS | all hosts PSS | gateway RSS |
|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0 | idle | 108.6 MB | 134.2 MB | 108.6 MB | 93.8 MB |
| 1 | 1 | after the turn | 125.1 MB | 153.6 MB | 125.1 MB | 94.4 MB |
| 10 | 0 | idle | 73.4 MB | 120.7 MB | 734.2 MB | 98.3 MB |
| 10 | 1 | after the turn | 87.8 MB | 141.0 MB | 877.7 MB | 112.9 MB |
| 25 | 0 | idle | 65.2 MB | 117.3 MB | 1,630.8 MB | 107.2 MB |
| 25 | 1 | after the turn | 74.6 MB | 130.8 MB | 1,864.5 MB | 131.0 MB |
| 40 | 0 | idle | 67.0 MB | 121.5 MB | 2,681.1 MB | 111.2 MB |
| 40 | 1 | after the turn | 72.2 MB | 129.3 MB | 2,888.4 MB | 134.4 MB |
| 10 | 10 | after ten turns | 94.4 MB | 147.7 MB | 943.8 MB | 109.9 MB |

The last row is a separate run from a fresh gateway: ten people, each asking ten
questions in one conversation, every question a real tool call.

Two things the table shows:

- **A host shares most of itself.** At 40 hosts, a host's own share (PSS) is
  72 MB against 129 MB resident. The runtime's code pages are mapped once and
  shared, so the per-host cost falls as hosts are added, and levels off at
  about 70–75 MB from 25 hosts on.
- **The gateway is not the cost.** It held 134 MB with 40 people signed in and
  streaming.

### 200 people

A host grows with its conversation. At 10 hosts, nine more turns each added
6.6 MB of PSS: **about 0.7 MB a turn**. That is a lower bound. The scripted
answers are a sentence long and each search returns five rows, while a real
DeepSeek answer, and a report preview of twenty rows, is longer.

Scaled from the measurements:

| | per host | 200 hosts |
|---|---:|---:|
| Measured floor: short conversations (72–94 MB PSS from 25 hosts on) | ~75–95 MB | **~15–19 GB** |
| Long conversations: 50 turns at a measured 0.7 MB, with headroom for real answers (×3) | ~200 MB | ~40 GB |
| Ceiling: every host at its 256 MB heap cap, plus its ~70 MB not on the heap | ~330 MB | ~65 GB |

The rest of the server holds the following:

- the gateway: 134 MB at 40 people, about 0.5 GB allowed for 200;
- the two Loco backends and their front ends: about 1 GB;
- PostgreSQL with 200 connections: 2–4 GB;
- the operating system and page cache: about 4 GB.

So **200 people active at once fit in 32 GB**, with room for most of them to
hold long conversations. **64 GB** is for every one of them sitting at the
heap ceiling at the same time, and a host stops there by design. That is
lower than the 40–70 GB estimated before anything was measured: the runtime
shares far more between hosts than an estimate per process assumed.

Two limits on what this shows:

- **It was measured up to 40 hosts.** That is what a 16 GB machine holds with
  the rest of the stack beside it. The 200 column assumes the per-host cost
  stays where it settled from 25 hosts on; it was falling, not rising, as
  hosts were added.
- **Only the model is scripted.** DeepSeek's own latency does not change the
  memory a host holds; a longer answer does, and that is the ×3 above.

Run `bun run load` on the server that will carry it before relying on any of
this. The script refuses to start a step with less than `--min-available-mb`
free.

### The three controls

- **`CHAT_HOST_IDLE_MINUTES`** (30). A host with no traffic for that long is
  stopped, and its session log stays on disk. The next message starts it
  again in about a second. Signed-in people are rarely all active, and an
  idle one costs nothing.
- **`CHAT_HOST_HEAP_MB`** (256). The heap ceiling given to each host's Node.
  One runaway conversation fails its own host, which restarts, rather than
  the machine.
- **`CHAT_MAX_HOSTS`** (0 means derived). At most this many hosts run at
  once. The next person waits, with a stated position, rather than pushing the
  machine into swap. The default is three quarters of the machine's memory
  divided by the larger of `MEASURED_HOST_RSS_MB` (`gateway/hosts.ts`) and 90%
  of the heap ceiling, so it is sized from what a host was measured to cost.

## Running it

In a generated project, `docker compose up` starts the chat with everything
else, behind nginx on one origin: the application at `/`, the chat at
`/chat/`. In the orchestrator (`app-and-report-with-ai-rust`), `./start.sh`
generates `CHAT_AUTH_SECRET` and the `SSO_SIGNING_KEY` / `SSO_PUBLIC_KEY` pair
once, and serves the chat at `/chat` beside `/app` and `/report`.

Natively, with the application and the reporting platform running:

```bash
bun install
cp .env.example .env      # in a generated project; fill CHAT_AUTH_SECRET,
                          # SSO_SIGNING_KEY and DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
bun gateway/server.ts     # :3100, under CHAT_BASE_PATH (/chat)
```

Every variable `gateway/config.ts` reads is in a generated project's
`.env.example`, with that project's ports filled in. Three of them must never
change once set:

- `CHAT_AUTH_SECRET` — changing it ends every chat session;
- `SSO_SIGNING_KEY` — replacing it without its `SSO_PUBLIC_KEY` makes every
  reporting sign-in a bad signature;
- `CHAT_DATABASE_URL` — this must be a database **of its own**, never the
  application's: the reporting platform reads every schema of the database it
  reports on, so chat sessions stored there would become reportable rows. The
  gateway creates the database on first start when it is missing.

Hosts need Node 22.19 or later (`CHAT_NODE_BIN`). The image installs it.

## Tests

```bash
bun run type-check
bun run test                 # unit: config, cookies, crypto, the proxy's filters
bun run test:composition     # the composition gate — no package outside the allowlist
```

Against a running stack (application, reporting platform, the gateway behind
nginx with `CHAT_TRUST_PROXY=1`, and `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL` pointed at
`tests/support/messages-recorder.ts`):

```bash
bun test tests/security      # the gateway's refusals, and the platform's half of sign-on
bun test tests/e2e --timeout 180000
bun run load -- --app-db postgres://…/<app>_development --steps 1,10,25,40
```

`tests/security/gateway.test.ts` covers the refusals:

- every route and stream refused without a session;
- one person's view id is a 404 for another;
- the mux and settings filters;
- `Origin` and `Host` checks;
- hosts unreachable from outside loopback.

`tests/security/reporting-assertion.test.ts` signs with the gateway's own
`signAssertion` and covers:

- replay, a foreign key, an edited payload, expiry, audience and a
  deactivated account, each refused;
- role sync.

The end-to-end suite drives Chromium through the following:

- sign in once;
- open a record from the conversation;
- save it in the embedded form, and see the `[Application]` event;
- the conflict dialog inside the chat;
- a report in a card;
- the reporting page embedded, with no second sign-in.

**Only the model's words are scripted.** A run against the live DeepSeek
model needs `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`. Where there is none, it is reported as not
run, never imitated.

# installation, and its own profiles install with `nodeLinker: hoisted`. The
# isolated linker Bun uses for workspaces would hide @deepseek-ai/* from our
# plugins, so this package installs hoisted.
[install]
linker = "hoisted"

/chat-deepseek/profile/business.patch.ym:
# The business chat's composition: the shipped Web surface (`dsh-base` +
# `dsh-web-app`) narrowed to a person talking to one application.
#
# Passed to every host as `--patch`, after the bundle, profile and home layers,
# so it is the last word and nothing a profile on disk holds can widen it.
# Our plugins are packages of this workspace (`plugins/*`), resolved by name.
#
# Three things happen here, in order:
#
# 1. Every row that gives the agent, or the browser, a way off the business
#    surface is disabled: shells and subprocesses, the sandbox, terminals,
#    workspace files and uploads, web fetch and search, MCP, programmatic tool
#    calling (it runs model-written code), sub-agents and workflows, the plugin
#    manager, the configuration editor and every settings screen that writes the
#    composition, other model providers and account sign-in, and telemetry that
#    leaves the machine. The gateway proxies this host's whole HTTP surface to
#    the person, so a Host API left mounted is an API the person can call.
# 2. The four shipped agent presets are disabled and one is inserted: the
#    `business` preset, whose only tools are the application's (`business-tools`)
#    and `skill`, which reads the skills written for it.
# 3. The model is fixed: DeepSeek, by the key in the host's environment.
#
# `tests/composition/check-composition.ts` composes this file over the shipped
# bundles and fails on any enabled row outside its allowlist, and boots a host
# to confirm the agent's tool catalog is exactly the business tools plus `skill`.

# ── 1. Off the business surface ──────────────────────────────────────────────

# Package management, live reconfiguration and the editors that write the profile.
- id: plugin-manager
  disabled: true
- id: tool-plugin-manager
  disabled: true
- id: hmr
  disabled: true
# `settings`, `settings-controller` and `config-editor` stay: the client reads
# its display preferences through them (`ui-chat`'s transcript mode, below),
# and the settings service will not start without the editor that persists it.
# Every write method is refused by the gateway for every caller
# (`REMOTE_ALLOWLIST.settings` in gateway/proxy.ts) and the editor has no Remote
# namespace of its own, so the person can read what is configured and change
# nothing.
- id: permission
  disabled: true

# Processes, shells and the sandbox they run in.
- id: subprocess
  disabled: true
- id: sandbox
  disabled: true
- id: bash-sandbox
  disabled: true
- id: pwsh-sandbox
  disabled: true
- id: shell-env
  disabled: true
- id: jobs
  disabled: true
- id: ptc-runtime
  disabled: true

# The web and external tool servers.
- id: web
  disabled: true
- id: web-search-deepseek
  disabled: true
- id: web-fetch-http
  disabled: true
- id: mcp-resources
  disabled: true

# Delegation and long-running goals.
- id: subagent
  disabled: true
- id: subagent-spawn-in-process
  disabled: true
- id: subagent-fork-in-process
  disabled: true
- id: subagent-model-selection-settings
  disabled: true
- id: goal
  disabled: true
- id: goal-round-driver
  disabled: true

# Other model routes and account sign-in: the deployment's key is the only route.
- id: llm-pi-ai
  disabled: true
- id: deepseek-account
  disabled: true
- id: llm-deepseek-account
  disabled: true
- id: account-controller
  disabled: true
- id: ui-settings-account
  disabled: true

# Telemetry and feedback that leave the machine.
- id: otel
  disabled: true
- id: session-telemetry-otel
  disabled: true
- id: message-feedback
  disabled: true
- id: ui-message-feedback
  disabled: true

# Host APIs over the machine: terminals, workspace files, the workspace, jobs,
# opening native applications, picking directories, the Cordis runners.
# `fs`, `sandbox-policy`, `attachment-local` and `file-upload` stay: the session
# API will not start without them, and they serve message attachments, not the
# machine — no agent tool reads a file and no browser API browses one.
- id: terminal-controller

- id: workspace-files

# The chat's own session folders. Its documents directory is the person's host

- id: workspace-changes

- id: job-controller
  disabled: true
- id: file-reference-local
  disabled: true
- id: open-in-app
  disabled: true
- id: ui-open-in-app
  disabled: true
- id: directory-picker
  disabled: true
- id: plugin-inventory

  disabled: true

# ── 2. One agent preset ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

- id: agent-preset-registry
  config:
    default: business
- id: preset-standard
  disabled: true
- id: preset-ptc
  disabled: true
- id: preset-minimal
  disabled: true
- id: preset-cordis
  disabled: true

- insert:
    - id: preset-business
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset'
      config:
        id: business
        order: 1
        plugins:
          - id: persona
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona'
            config:
              prefix: >-
                You are the business assistant for this application, working for the person
                signed in to this chat. You act only through your tools, and only ever as that
                person: you can find and read what they are allowed to see, run the reports they
                are allowed to run, and open the application's own screens for them to create,
                change and approve records in. You never change a record yourself.
              complete: true
              includeRuntimeContext: false
          - id: agent-instructions
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-instructions'
            config:
              maxBytes: 65536
          - id: skill-filesystem
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem'
            config:
              includeDefaultRoots: false
              customSkillDirs: !!js "[process.env.CHAT_SKILLS_DIR].filter(Boolean)"
              watch: false
          - id: tool-skill
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-skill'
          - id: compaction
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              compaction: true
              toolResultPruner: true
            config:
              - id: compaction-basic
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic'
              - id: tool-result-pruner
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-tool-result-pruner'
                config:
                  thresholdChars: 8192
                  headChars: 4096
                  tailChars: 1024
          - id: business-tools
            name: '@appwithai/chat-business-tools'

# The cards that render the business tools' results in the conversation: the
# application's own screens and the reports. A top-level row, because a row is
# what puts a package's browser half (`dsh.client`) into the Web client.
- insert:
    - id: business-nodes
      name: '@appwithai/chat-business-nodes'

# ── 3. The model ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

- id: agent-default-model
  config:
    provider: deepseek-official
    model: !!js "process.env.CHAT_DEEPSEEK_MODEL || 'deepseek-flash'"

- id: system-prompt
  config:
    personaPrefix: >-
      You are the business assistant for this application.
    personaSuffix: ''

# Finished turns stay unfolded. Harness folds a completed turn's steps under
# "Completed in 1s" in every mode but `verbose`, and in this chat the steps are
# the application's own screens: a form folded away is a form the person was
# told is open and cannot see. Fixed here because the person's own patch layer
# is reset on every host start (gateway/hosts.ts).
- id: ui-chat
  config:
    transcriptView: verbose
/chat-deepseek/skills/asking-questions-i:
---
name: asking-questions-in-plain-language
description: Turning a question in plain language into the right report or search.
whenToUse: When the person asks a business question in their own words and it is not obvious which tool answers it.
---

# Asking questions in plain language

Map the question to the narrowest tool that answers it truthfully:

| The question is about | Use |
|---|---|
| one named record ("what's the status of Acme's order?") | `search_records`, then `get_record_summary` |
| a short list ("open tickets assigned to me") | `search_records` with filters |
| a number across records ("how many", "total", "by month") | `search_reports`, then `run_approved_report` |
| doing something ("approve", "add", "change") | open the screen; see the other skills |

There is no free-form query. Questions are answered by the saved reports the
business has agreed on; when none fits, say what reports exist that come
closest, and that a new report would need to be created on the reporting
platform.
/chat-deepseek/skills/charts-and-dashboa:
---
name: charts-and-dashboards
description: Charts that belong to a report, and the reporting platform's dashboards.
whenToUse: When the person asks for a chart, a graph, a visual, or a dashboard.
---

# Charts and dashboards

A report may have a **chart** drawn from the same saved query. When it does,
the report card offers **Chart and report page**, which opens the reporting
platform's own page for that report — chart included — inside the
conversation.

Dashboards live in the reporting platform. The person can open
`/report` in a tab; they are already signed in there.

Do not describe a chart's shape from the first rows of a table: the preview is
a page of rows, not the whole series.
/chat-deepseek/skills/creating-records/S:
---
name: creating-records
description: Opening the application's new-record form with open_create_form.
whenToUse: When the person wants to add, create, register or enter a new record.
---

# Creating records

`open_create_form` opens the application's own **New** form for an entity
inside the conversation. The person fills it in and presses **Create**.

- Tell them in one line what the form is for and any field the application
  will insist on (a summary or the entity's help says which).
- Nothing exists until they press Create. The chat then posts an
  `[Application] … created` message with the record's label and status — only
  then is it real.
- Validation, defaults, numbering and rules are the application's. If the form
  refuses, the reason is shown in the form; help them fix that field.
- Line items are created from their parent record, not on their own.
/chat-deepseek/skills/finding-records/SK:
---
name: finding-records
description: Searching for records with search_records and reading one with get_record_summary.
whenToUse: When the person asks to find, list, look up or check records.
---

# Finding records

- Name the entity as the application does. `search_records` accepts the screen
  name ("Sales Order"), the singular, or the table name; if it refuses, its
  message lists the entities this person can see.
- Use `text` for "anything mentioning…" and `filters` for exact values
  (`{"status": "open"}`). Filters take column names, which appear as field
  labels in results; ask `get_record_summary` when unsure.
- Results are paged (default 20, up to 50). Say how many matched in total, not
  just how many you show.
- Each row has a `ref`. Keep it to open or summarise that record later; never
  show it to the person.
- For totals, counts by status or anything across many records, use a report
  instead (see *running-reports*).
/chat-deepseek/skills/roles-and-access/S:
---
name: roles-and-access
description: What a role means here, and how to explain a refused request.
whenToUse: When a tool answers 'Not permitted', or the person asks what they or someone else can see or do.
---

# Roles and access

The application decides access in three steps, on every request:

1. which **screens** the person's role may open;
2. which **operations** (read, create, update, delete) the role has on each
   entity;
3. which **workflow moves** the role may make.

The reporting platform separately decides which **tables** a role's reports
may read.

The assistant has no access of its own: it sees and opens exactly what the
person can. So when something is refused:

- say they do not have permission for that, in their words ("you can't edit
  accounts"), not a code;
- suggest their administrator if they believe they should have it;
- do not retry, rephrase the request to get around it, or try another tool.
/chat-deepseek/skills/running-reports/SK:
---
name: running-reports
description: Finding and running saved reports with search_reports and run_approved_report.
whenToUse: When the person asks a question across many records: totals, counts, trends, breakdowns, lists by criteria.
---

# Running reports

Reports are the business's agreed answers: saved queries on the reporting
platform, each checked against the person's data permissions when it runs.

1. `search_reports` with a few words from the question. It returns only reports
   this person can run.
2. `run_approved_report` with the chosen report's id. The conversation shows
   the report as a paged table; you receive the columns, the row count and the
   first rows.
3. Answer from what you received, and say where the full result is (the card:
   pages, CSV/XLSX/PDF export, and the platform's report page).

If no report fits, say so plainly. Do not compute business figures from a
handful of searched records and present them as totals.
/chat-deepseek/skills/updating-records-a:
---
name: updating-records-and-conflicts
description: Editing a record with open_update_form, and what the conflict and final-state messages mean.
whenToUse: When the person wants to change a record, or reports a 'changed while you were editing' or 'final' message.
---

# Updating records, and conflicts

`open_update_form` opens the record's edit form. The person changes it and
saves.

## Two people, one record

Every save says which version of the record it started from. If someone else
saved in between, the application refuses with **"This record was changed
while you were editing it"** and shows who changed it, when, and the fields
that differ — theirs beside the person's. Two choices:

- **Refresh to latest** — discard the person's edits and load the record as it
  now stands. Safe; nothing they typed is kept.
- **Overwrite with my changes** — save the person's values over the other
  edit. Deliberate; the other person's changes to those fields are lost.

It is the person's call. Explain the difference; do not choose for them.

## Final states

A record whose status is a **final** state (Closed Won, Paid, Cancelled…) is a
completed transaction. The application refuses every change to it — for every
user, administrators included — and the edit form will not open. Say so; do not
look for a way around it.
/chat-deepseek/skills/using-the-applicat:
---
name: using-the-application
description: How the business application is organised and how the assistant works inside it.
whenToUse: At the start of a conversation, or when the person asks what the assistant or the application can do.
---

# Using the application

The application is organised as **entities** (Account, Sales Order, Ticket, …),
each with its own screen — a list, then a record. Some entities have a
**workflow**: a status that moves along drawn steps, some of which are *final*.
Line items (an order's lines, an invoice's lines) have no screen of their own;
they appear inside their parent record.

What the person sees depends on their **role**. The assistant sees exactly the
same: if they cannot open an entity in the application, the assistant cannot
search it either.

The assistant works in three ways:

1. **Reads** — searches and record summaries, answered in the conversation.
2. **Screens** — the application's own screens, opened inside the conversation
   for the person to act in.
3. **Reports** — saved reports from the reporting platform, shown as tables
   with export and the platform's report page.

The assistant never changes data itself.
/chat-deepseek/skills/workflows-and-appr:
---
name: workflows-and-approvals
description: Moving a record through its workflow with request_approval.
whenToUse: When the person wants to approve, reject, submit, close, cancel or otherwise move a record's status.
---

# Workflows and approvals

A record with a workflow has a status that moves only along the steps the
business drew. `get_record_summary` lists the moves available **from the
current status**; any other move does not exist.

To move a record, call `request_approval` with the record's ref and the target
status from that list. It opens the record at its workflow bar with that move
selected; the person confirms it in the application.

- The application decides whether *this person* may make that move. If their
  role may not, the confirmation is refused and the screen says so — that is a
  permission, not an error.
- Two people moving the same record at once: one move lands, the other is
  refused as a conflict.
- A final status has no moves. The record's transaction is complete.
- After the move, the `[Application]` message reports the new status; state it.

specification:
  name: CEDM Specification Manifest
  version: 0.1.0
  status: draft

purpose: >-
  Provide a machine-readable, implementation-neutral semantic model for
  enterprise business applications.

layers:
  - domain/entities
  - specification

artifacts:
  canonical:
    - domain/entities/index.yaml
    - domain/entities/*.yaml
  semantics:
    - specification/validation.yaml
    - specification/lifecycle.yaml
    - specification/relationship-semantics.yaml
    - specification/business-rules.yaml
    - specification/aggregate-boundaries.yaml
    - specification/reporting.yaml
    - specification/integration.yaml
    - specification/authorization.yaml

implementationTargets:
  - relationalDatabase
  - sql
  - cds
  - jsonSchema
  - openapi
  - graphql
  - typescript
  - java
  - rust
  - python
  - workflowEngine
  - uiMetadata

conformance:
  entityRegistryIsAuthoritative: true
  implementationMustNotInventDomainSemantics: true
  generatedArtifactsAreNonCanonical: true
/specification/aggregate-boundaries.yaml:
specification:
  name: CEDM Aggregate Boundaries
  version: 0.1.0
  status: draft

aggregates:
  - name: ERP
    root: ERP
    members: [Organization, Party, Location, Product, BusinessProcess, Workflow, Document]
  - name: SalesOrder
    root: SalesOrder
    members: [SalesOrderLine]
  - name: PurchaseOrder
    root: PurchaseOrder
    members: [PurchaseOrderLine]
  - name: Inventory
    root: Warehouse
    members: [InventoryLocation, InventoryBalance, InventoryMovement]
  - name: Yard
    root: Yard
    members: [YardBlock, YardBay, YardTier, YardSlot, ContainerMovement]
  - name: RepairEstimate
    root: RepairEstimate
    members: [RepairEstimateLine]
  - name: AccountingEntry
    root: JournalEntry
    members: [JournalEntryLine]

rules:
  - id: AGG-001
    rule: Aggregate members are modified through their aggregate root unless a domain rule explicitly permits independent lifecycle management.
  - id: AGG-002
    rule: Cross-aggregate references must not imply ownership.
  - id: AGG-003
    rule: Transaction boundaries should align with aggregate invariants.
/specification/application-profile.yaml:
# CEDM Application Profile
# What an application built on CEDM adds to the domain model, in CEDM's terms.
#
# CEDM describes the domain: entities, relationships, lifecycles, invariants and
# help, independent of any implementation. An application built on it also has
# to say how the domain is presented, who may do what, which rules execute,
# which processes run and which questions it answers. This profile is where
# those are specified, so an application model stays a CEDM document rather
# than a second, private language.
#
# The normative schema is language/cedm/cedm-model.schema.json; the reference is
# language/cedm/README.md. A CEDM application model is lowered into the model
# document every generator compiles (language/yaml/eml.schema.json).
specification:
  name: CEDM Application Profile
  version: 1.0.0
  status: draft

applicationModel:
  document:
    required: [cedm]
    keys:
      cedm: Version of the application model ("1.0").
      application: Name, version, description, namespace, and the catalog domain it serves.
      imports: Library entities (domain/entities) and application modules brought into the model.
      enums: Value lists shared by several attributes.
      entities: Entities in the CEDM entity shape, declared or refining an imported one.
      ui: Dashboard categories.
      authorization: Permissions (authorization.yaml), granted per role.
      hooks: Lifecycle handlers the backend dispatches to around every read and write.
      hookFlows: The documented order of an entity's hooks.
      triggers: External events and schedules that call a handler.
      reports: Read-only questions the application serves.
      rules: Executable business rules, compiled to decision graphs.
      processes: Multi-step processes run on a write (sagas), compiled to BPMN.

  imports:
    entity:
      description: >-
        Brings the canonical definition of a library entity. An imported entity
        also brings every entity its required relationships (cardinality 1 or
        1..*) and required reference attributes point at, recursively; an
        optional reference to an entity the application does not contain is
        not generated, and is reported.
      options:
        include: Keep only these attributes and relationships (the identity is always kept).
        exclude: Drop these attributes and relationships.
    module:
      description: >-
        Brings everything another application model declares. Domain
        applications share one common foundation module this way.
      resolution: [<name>.cedm.yaml beside the importing model, applications/<name>.cedm.yaml]
    refinement: >-
      An entity declared in the model with the name of an imported one refines
      it: its keys replace the imported ones; attributes and relationships merge
      by name.

  entityExtensions:
    ui:
      icon: A lucide icon id drawn on the dashboard card, window heading and navigation.
      label: The name the screens show.
    persistence:
      prefix: Table prefix (bus or sys).
      softDelete: Retire rows by setting deleted_at.
      audited: Keep an audit trail.
      concurrency: >-
        How two people editing one record are reconciled. optimistic (the
        default) refuses a save made against a version someone else has
        replaced and offers refresh or overwrite; last-write-wins accepts a save
        that names no version. A record in a final state is closed either way.
      indexes: Composite indexes beyond those derived from unique and reference attributes.
    aggregateRoot: >-
      The aggregate root of a line item, where no ownership aggregate
      relationship on the root states it. A member gets no window of its own;
      it appears as a tab inside its root's.

  attributeExtensions:
    column: The physical column, where it is not the snake_case of the name (or id, for the identity key).
    values: Inline value list; the attribute becomes a dropdown.
    enumName: The name an inline value list is published under (default <Entity><Attribute>).
    enum: A shared value list from the model's enums.
    keyType: The stored type of a reference's key (default string).
    ui: The control to draw the attribute with.
    format: How the value is shown or checked.
    comment: A note shown beside the attribute in the model viewer.

  relationshipExtensions:
    inverseCardinality: >-
      How many source records relate to one target. Defaults to 1 for a to-many
      relationship; a to-one relationship that states none is the many side of
      a one-to-many owned by its target.
    foreignKey: >-
      The attribute holding the key: on the source for a to-one relationship,
      on the target for a to-many one. Found by name when omitted and created
      when none exists; false says the key is kept elsewhere.
    label: The relationship's name in the generated application.

  invariantExtensions:
    violatedWhen: >-
      The condition under which the invariant is broken, in the rules engine's
      expression language over physical columns. An invariant with one compiles
      to a validation rule; one without is documentation, carried into the
      generated application's bundled specification.
    events: Lifecycle events the compiled rule runs on (default beforeCreate, beforeUpdate).

compilation:
  names:
    attributes: camelCase in the model; snake_case columns in the application.
    identity: A single identity key is stored in the column id.
  types:
    preserved: [uuid, string, integer, decimal, money, boolean, date, datetime, object]
    mapped:
      enum: string, with the attribute's value list
      reference: the keyType (default string), as a foreign key
      currency_code: string(3)
      country_code: string(2)
      locale: string(35)
      timezone: string(64)
      value_object: json
    maxLength: Written as the length of a string column.
  relationships:
    toOne: >-
      A foreign key on the source, named <relationship>_id unless an attribute
      already holds it. Its target is stored explicitly wherever the column's
      name would not resolve to it (delivery_location_id → Location).
    toMany: The other half of a to-one relationship on the target, or a key on the target.
    pairs: >-
      Two relationships that name each other as inverse, or the only two
      between a pair of entities where one is to-many, are one relationship.
    cardinality: n..* with n > 1 is enforced as 1..*.
  ownership:
    aggregate: The target becomes a line item of the source (no window; a tab inside the root's).
  lifecycle:
    states: The state machine's states, in the order listed.
    transitions: Each transition's action becomes its trigger, which authorization may grant.
    terminal: The machine's final states.
  help:
    structured: The fields are joined, in the order written, into one paragraph.
  authorization:
    allow: Compiles to a role grant on an operation or transition.
    deny: Refused — the application's grants are additive; grant only to the roles that may act.
    scope: Refused — the application grants per role.
  extends: >-
    A specialisation carries its parent's attributes and relationships (all but
    the parent's identity).

applications:
  description: >-
    Each catalog domain is its own application, under applications/, and every
    application imports the common module (applications/common.cedm.yaml) for
    the foundation every domain shares. Every generated application bundles the
    common specification — specification/, schema/ and domains/ — under cedm/,
    with the library entities and modules it used.

rules:
  - id: APP-001
    rule: An application model must lower to a model document that satisfies the model language's schema and checker.
  - id: APP-002
    rule: Lowering must not drop a construct silently; what cannot be generated is reported.
  - id: APP-003
    rule: An explicit reference target is authoritative over any target derived from a column name.
/specification/authorization.yaml:
specification:
  name: CEDM Authorization Semantics
  version: 0.1.0
  status: draft

authorization:
  principles:
    - Authorization is separate from authentication.
    - Permissions may depend on party, role, organization, resource, action, and context.
    - Domain invariants cannot be bypassed by authorization.

  permission:
    fields:
      - action
      - resource
      - subject
      - scope
      - effect
    actions:
      - create
      - read
      - update
      - delete
      - approve
      - submit
      - post
      - cancel
      - execute

  policy:
    effects: [allow, deny]
    defaultEffect: deny
/specification/business-logic.yaml:
# CEDM Business Logic
#
# What an entity states so that an application generated from it enforces the
# domain's rules and runs its workflows, without a developer re-reading prose.
# Three constructs carry it, each written in the entity's own file:
#
#   lifecycle   the states of a status attribute and the moves between them
#   invariants  business rules; one with `violatedWhen` is executable
#   processes   workflows that run when a rule fires (domains/processes/)
#
# `tools/validate.py` enforces BL-001…BL-014; the generators compile what
# conforms: a lifecycle to a state machine (`sys_workflow_transitions`, which
# every write to the status column is checked against), an executable invariant
# to a validation rule (`/admin/rules`), a process to a workflow definition
# (`/admin/workflow-definitions`). A generated application also ships tests for
# each one, so a rule that stops being enforced fails a build rather than a
# customer.
specification:
  name: CEDM Business Logic
  version: 1.0.0
  status: draft
  appliesTo: [domain/entities, domains/processes, specification/lifecycle.yaml, specification/business-rules.yaml]

lifecycle:
  where: "An entity's top-level `lifecycle` key."
  keys:
    attribute: "The enum attribute the lifecycle governs — `status`, `state` or `stage`, in that order of preference."
    states: Exactly the attribute's values. A state the lifecycle does not name is a value the application accepts on create and can never leave.
    initial: The state a new record starts in. It is the attribute's default where the entity states one.
    terminal: States with no outgoing move. A record in one is finished; correcting it is a new record or a reversal, never an edit.
    transitions: "Each `{from, to, action}`; `action` is the command that makes the move and is unique per `(from, to)`."
  guarantees:
    - Topology is enforced for every caller, the master role included. A move the diagram never drew is a move that does not exist.
    - A transition may carry `authorization` (roles that may make it) and `guard` (a condition over the record).
  derivation: >-
    Where an entity states only its status values, tools/derive_business_logic.py draws the lifecycle
    from them: the values are sorted into a starting run, detours that are left and returned to
    (SUSPENDED, ON_HOLD, BLOCKED, INACTIVE…), ends that mean it ran its course (COMPLETED, CLOSED…)
    and ends that mean it did not or is no longer in use (CANCELLED, REJECTED, RETIRED…). A derived
    lifecycle is a default an author refines by editing the entity file; the tool never overwrites one.

rules:
  where: "An entity's `invariants`; an item with `violatedWhen` is executable."
  keys:
    id: "Unique in the specification; derived ones are `<ENTITY>-EXE-NNN`."
    rule: The rule as a business reader states it.
    violatedWhen: A condition over the record, true when the rule is broken, in the rules engine's expression language.
    message: What the person who broke it reads.
    severity: error (refuses the write) — the default; warning and info are carried and not enforced.
    events: beforeCreate and beforeUpdate unless stated.
  expression:
    identifiers: The entity's columns, snake_case, exactly as the generated table names them.
    literals: numbers, double-quoted strings, true, false, null
    operators: [==, "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=", and, or, not]
    nullSafety: "A comparison against a column that may be empty names the emptiness first (`x != null and x < 0`); an unguarded one is refused by BL-008."
  derived:
    - id: dates
      rule: "An end date is not earlier than its start (`startDate`/`endDate`, `effectiveFrom`/`effectiveTo`, \u2026)."
    - id: quantities
      rule: "A quantity, amount, price, cost, total, fee, charge or rate is not negative \u2014 except on entities that are signed by convention (journals, ledgers, adjustments, movements)."
    - id: percentages
      rule: "A percentage is between 0 and 100."
    - id: reasons
      rule: "A record that is cancelled, rejected, held, suspended, blocked, failed, reversed or voided states why, where the entity has an attribute for it."
    - id: stamps
      rule: "A record that is completed, closed, approved, posted, cancelled, shipped, delivered or retired states when, where the entity has a date attribute for it."

processes:
  where: domains/processes/<domain>.yaml, folded into the domain's application.
  contract: "A process names the entity whose change starts it (`entity`, `trigger: rule`), the condition (the rule that fires it) and its steps. It is one of the saga step types the generated backend runs."
  firing: "A process runs when a rule's `trigger-workflow` action names it. It is never started by being defined, so a process with no rule is documentation and BL-012 says so."

checks:
  - id: BL-001
    severity: error
    rule: "A lifecycle's `states` are exactly the governed attribute's values."
  - id: BL-002
    severity: error
    rule: "`initial` is a state, and `terminal` states are states."
  - id: BL-003
    severity: error
    rule: "Every transition goes from a state to a state, and no two share `(from, to)`."
  - id: BL-004
    severity: error
    rule: "A terminal state has no outgoing transition."
  - id: BL-005
    severity: error
    rule: "Every state is reachable from `initial`."
  - id: BL-006
    severity: error
    rule: "Every non-terminal state can reach a terminal state, or the lifecycle declares no terminal state."
  - id: BL-007
    severity: error
    rule: "Every executable invariant has a message and a unique id."
  - id: BL-008
    severity: error
    rule: "A `violatedWhen` uses only the entity's columns, literals and the listed operators, and guards a nullable column before comparing it."
  - id: BL-009
    severity: error
    rule: "A `violatedWhen` that names a state names one the lifecycle declares."
  - id: BL-010
    severity: error
    rule: "The record's initial state does not break an executable invariant \u2014 a new record must be creatable."
  - id: BL-011
    severity: warning
    rule: "An entity with a status enum and no lifecycle says so; it accepts any move."
  - id: BL-012
    severity: warning
    rule: "A process no rule triggers is documentation."
  - id: BL-013
    severity: error
    rule: "A process's steps name entities and fields that exist."
  - id: BL-014
    severity: error
    rule: "Every domain with transaction entities defines at least one process."
/specification/business-rules.yaml:
specification:
  name: CEDM Business Rule Semantics
  version: 0.2.0
  status: draft

rule:
  requiredFields:
    - id
    - rule
  optionalFields:
    - severity
    - appliesWhen
    - enforcement
    - message

  severity:
    values: [error, warning, info]
    default: error

  enforcement:
    values:
      - validation
      - workflow
      - authorization
      - persistence
      - calculation
      - integration
      - reporting

  principles:
    - Rules express domain meaning independently of implementation technology.
    - A rule may be enforced in more than one implementation layer.
    - Derived calculations must declare their source attributes and units where material.
    - Cross-entity rules belong to the domain rule layer rather than a single entity when they span aggregates.
    - Every existing and newly created CEDM entity is subject to mandatory workflow-impact reconciliation.
    - Any entity create or update MUST inspect all inbound and outbound relationships, lifecycle transitions, workflows, business processes, business rules, aggregate boundaries, and dependent entities affected by the change.
    - If an entity change changes the meaning, lifecycle, state transition, relationship, invariant, responsibility, or workflow participation of another entity, that dependent entity MUST be updated in the same semantic change set.
    - Entity help MUST explain not only the entity or field in isolation, but also its role in relevant workflows and its relationship to other affected entities.
    - Workflow-impact reconciliation applies retroactively to all existing entities and prospectively to every new entity added to CEDM.
    - An entity update is incomplete if its resulting definition cannot support every applicable CEDM workflow consistently with the definitions of the other participating entities.
    - Workflow, lifecycle, business-rule, aggregate-boundary, domain-catalog, and entity-index definitions MUST be reconciled whenever an entity change affects them.
    - Historical/event entities MUST be distinguished from current-state entities; a workflow must not overwrite historical facts when a corrective event or transition is required.

  mandatoryEntityChangeProtocol:
    appliesTo: [existing_entities, new_entities]
    severity: error
    steps:
      - id: ECP-001
        rule: Read the complete entity definition and identify all fields, relationships, invariants, lifecycle states, and aggregate ownership semantics.
      - id: ECP-002
        rule: Identify all inbound and outbound entity dependencies, including direct references, inverse relationships, derived state, and workflow participation.
      - id: ECP-003
        rule: Trace every workflow and business process that creates, reads, updates, transitions, consumes, or retires the entity.
      - id: ECP-004
        rule: Identify downstream and upstream entities whose definitions, help, lifecycle, relationships, invariants, or workflow participation are affected.
      - id: ECP-005
        rule: Update every materially affected entity and cross-entity rule in the same semantic reconciliation pass.
      - id: ECP-006
        rule: Reconcile lifecycle and state transitions across all participating entities so that workflow preconditions and postconditions remain executable.
      - id: ECP-007
        rule: Reconcile workflow, business-process, business-rule, aggregate-boundary, domain-catalog, and entity-index specifications where applicable.
      - id: ECP-008
        rule: Verify that entity and field help explains workflow usage, relationship context, and interaction with other affected entities.
      - id: ECP-009
        rule: Validate cross-entity invariants, ownership boundaries, event/state semantics, and historical traceability after the change.
      - id: ECP-010
        rule: Do not mark an entity change complete until the affected workflow graph is semantically consistent.

  completionCriteria:
    entityChangeIsCompleteOnlyWhen:
      - entity_definition_is_consistent
      - field_help_is_domain_specific
      - relationship_help_is_domain_specific
      - lifecycle_is_consistent
      - workflow_participation_is_consistent
      - cross_entity_rules_are_consistent
      - aggregate_boundaries_are_consistent
      - historical_vs_current_state_semantics_are_consistent
      - affected_catalog_and_index_metadata_are_consistent
/specification/conformance.yaml:
specification:
  name: CEDM Conformance Profile
  version: 0.1.0
  status: draft

conformance:
  levels:
    level1:
      name: Structural
      requirements:
        - validYaml
        - registryComplete
        - requiredEntityFieldsPresent
        - uniqueEntityNames
        - uniqueIdentifiers
    level2:
      name: Relational
      requirements:
        - allRelationshipTargetsResolve
        - cardinalitiesValid
        - inverseRelationshipsResolve
        - inheritanceTargetsResolve
    level3:
      name: Semantic
      requirements:
        - lifecycleStatesResolve
        - invariantsHaveIdentifiers
        - businessRulesAreDeclarative
        - aggregateBoundariesResolve
    level4:

        - apiContractCanBeGenerated

/specification/dictionary-mapping.yaml:
# CEDM → Application Dictionary Mapping
#
# The Application Dictionary (the sys_* tables of a generated application) is
# what turns a domain model into screens: a window per entity, a tab and its
# fields, a column behind every field, a list of values behind every dropdown.
# This document says, normatively, which CEDM construct supplies every slot of
# it, which slots have a derivation rule where the specification is silent, and
# which are required. A CEDM specification that follows it supplies the whole
# dictionary: nothing a screen shows has to be invented by a generator.
#
# `tools/validate.py` enforces the required rows (DICT-*); `tools/dictionary_report.py`
# reports coverage. A generator reads the same rows: where one says "derived",
# the rule below is the rule, and a generator must not apply another.
specification:
  name: CEDM Application Dictionary Mapping
  version: 1.0.0
  status: draft
  appliesTo: [schema/cedm-entity.schema.yaml, specification/help-semantics.yaml]

principles:
  - The dictionary is derived from the specification and never the reverse; a label, an icon or a help text is written once, in the entity file.
  - A slot with no source in an entity file has a derivation rule here, or is not required.
  - Business screens speak in windows, tabs and fields. A dictionary table or column name (sys_table.name, sys_column.column_name) is storage, and is never a label.
  - Nothing is defaulted silently. A derivation is documented here, applied by every generator the same way, and reported by `dictionary_report.py`.

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Entity → window, tab, table
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
entity:
  window:
    name:
      source: ui.label
      derived: The entity name, split into words (SalesOrderLine → Sales Order Line).
      required: derived
    description:
      source: help.summary
      required: true
    help:
      source: help slots listed under `help.windowSlots`
      required: true
    icon:
      source: ui.icon
      required: true
      rule: A lucide icon id (https://lucide.dev), as published by the lucide release the generated frontend pins (0.312). Checked against tools/lucide-icons.txt.
    window_type:
      source: kind
      derived: The class of the kind (see kindClasses) gives M for master data and T for transactions.
      required: derived
    is_sales_transaction:
      source: kind class
      derived: true for a transaction whose entity belongs to the sales domain (namespace or kind begins with sales_ or commercial_).
      required: derived
  tab:
    name:
      source: ui.label
      derived: Same as the window for the top tab; the owning relationship's name for a line item's tab.
      required: derived
    description:
      source: description
      required: false
    help:
      source: help slots listed under `help.tabSlots`
      required: true
    is_read_only:
      source: kind class
      derived: true for an event (history is appended, never edited).
      required: derived
    is_insert_record:
      source: kind class
      derived: false for an event.
      required: derived
  table:
    description:
      source: help.summary
      required: true
    icon:
      source: ui.icon
      required: true
    is_document:
      source: kind class
      derived: true for a transaction or a line.
      required: derived
    is_changelog:
      source: audit | persistence.audited
      derived: true for a transaction, a line and an event; false otherwise.
      required: derived
    is_high_volume:
      source: ui.highVolume
      derived: true for an event; false otherwise.
      required: derived
  record:
    description: What identifies one record on a screen, a lookup or a list.
    source: ui.recordLabel
    derived: >-
      The first of: attributes named name, fullName, displayName, title, label, subject;
      firstName with lastName; code, reference, number; the first string attribute that is
      neither the identity nor a reference. Rule shared with the generator (identifierColumnNames).
    required: derived

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Attribute → column, field
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
attribute:
  column:
    name:
      source: ui.label
      derived: The attribute name, split into words.
      required: derived
    description:
      source: help.summary
      required: true
    sys_reference_id:
      source: type, values, target
      derived: >-
        uuid/reference with a target → lookup (Table Direct); enum or values → list;
        string, integer, decimal, money, boolean, date, datetime, object, text per the type map.
      required: derived
    field_length:
      source: maxLength
      required: false
    default_value:
      source: default
      required: false
    value_min:
      source: minimum
      required: false
    value_max:
      source: maximum
      required: false
    is_key:
      source: identity.key
      required: derived
    is_mandatory:
      source: required
      required: true
    is_updateable:
      source: immutable
      derived: false when immutable, when systemManaged, or when it is the identity.
      required: derived
    is_identifier:
      source: ui.recordLabel (on the entity)
      required: derived
    is_selection_column:
      source: ui.searchable
      derived: true for the record label, a unique attribute and a status attribute.
      required: derived
    is_encrypted:
      source: ui.sensitive
      required: false
    is_allow_copy:
      source: immutable | unique
      derived: false for an identity, a unique attribute and a system-managed one.
      required: derived
    format_pattern:
      source: format
      required: false
  field:
    name:
      source: ui.label
      derived: Same as the column.
      required: derived
    help:
      source: help slots listed under `help.fieldSlots`
      required: true
    group:
      source: ui.group
      derived: See `groups`.
      required: derived
    is_displayed:
      source: ui.form
      derived: false for a system-managed attribute and for an identity.
      required: derived
    is_displayed_grid:
      source: ui.grid
      derived: true for the record label, the status attribute, a unique attribute and up to six further attributes in declaration order; false for text and object attributes.
      required: derived
    is_read_only:
      source: ui.readOnly | immutable | systemManaged
      required: derived
    seq_no:
      source: declaration order
      required: derived
    num_lines:
      source: ui.lines
      derived: 1; 3 for a text attribute with maxLength above 500; 5 for an object attribute.
      required: derived
    column_span:
      source: ui.span
      derived: 2 for a text attribute, 1 otherwise.
      required: derived

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Field groups
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
groups:
  description: >-
    A tab's fields are laid out in named groups. An attribute states its group in
    `ui.group`; where it does not, the first matching rule below applies.
  order: [Identification, Classification, Status, Relationships, Dates, Amounts, Details, System]
  rules:
    - {group: System, when: systemManaged is true, or the name is createdAt, createdBy, updatedAt, updatedBy}
    - {group: Identification, when: the attribute is the identity, the record label, or is named code, number, reference, externalReference}
    - {group: Status, when: the attribute is named status, or is the attribute a lifecycle governs}
    - {group: Classification, when: an enum other than status, or named type, category, class, kind}
    - {group: Relationships, when: type is reference}
    - {group: Dates, when: type is date or datetime}
    - {group: Amounts, when: type is decimal, money or integer}
    - {group: Details, when: anything else}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Help
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
help:
  description: >-
    Help is written once, structured, in the entity file, and distributed to the
    dictionary slots below. A key outside this table is carried and shown in the
    generated manual but fills no slot.
  aliases:
    description: The two shapes of entity help in use are one contract. A key in the left column means the key on the right.
    purpose: businessMeaning
    whenUsed: usage
    howItRelates: relationshipContext
    lifecycleUsage: lifecycle
    commonProcesses: workflowContext
    commonExamples: example
  windowSlots: [businessMeaning, usage, workflowContext, example]
  tabSlots: [relationshipContext, lifecycle, propagation, concurrency]
  fieldSlots: [usage, businessMeaning, relationshipContext, workflowRole, requiredMeaning, optionalMeaning, validationGuidance, examples]
  summarySlot: summary
  carriedKeys:
    description: Keys that fill no slot but are part of the contract (shown in the generated manual). DICT-004 refuses any key in neither list.
    keys: [changePropagation, propagation, concurrency, operationalSemantics, workflowImpact, idempotency, optimizationContext, currentStateVsHistory, geospatialSemantics, operationalProcess, distinctions, synonyms, uiGuidance, lifecycleImpact, securityGuidance, valueSemantics, valueLabels, requiredMeaning, optionalMeaning, summary, purpose, whenUsed, howItRelates, lifecycleUsage, commonProcesses, commonExamples, targetMeaning, relationshipPurpose, cardinalityMeaning, navigationUse, context, workflowRole, example, examples, businessMeaning, usage, relationshipContext, lifecycle, validationGuidance, workflowContext]
  valueMeaning:
    source: help.valueSemantics
    slot: sys_ref_list.description
    description: One sentence per enumerated value, keyed by the value.
  relationshipHelp:
    description: A relationship's help becomes the help of the field that holds its key.
    slots: [summary, usage, cardinalityMeaning, context, workflowRole]

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Enumerations
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
enumerations:
  source: specification/enumeration-semantics.yaml
  dictionary:
    sys_reference: one list reference per enumeration
    sys_ref_list.value: the value
    sys_ref_list.name: valueLabels[value], else the value split into words
    sys_ref_list.description: help.valueSemantics[value]

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Rules a conforming specification satisfies (enforced by tools/validate.py)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
rules:
  - {id: DICT-001, severity: error, rule: Every entity has ui.icon, and it is a lucide icon id.}
  - {id: DICT-002, severity: error, rule: Every entity kind resolves to exactly one kind class.}
  - {id: DICT-003, severity: error, rule: Every entity has help.summary and help.businessMeaning (or its alias purpose).}
  - {id: DICT-004, severity: error, rule: Every help key is known (this document, help-semantics.yaml) so none is silently lost.}
  - {id: DICT-005, severity: error, rule: Every enumerated attribute gives help.valueSemantics for every one of its values, and for no other.}
  - {id: DICT-006, severity: error, rule: Every attribute has help.summary and help.usage.}
  - {id: DICT-007, severity: warning, rule: Every relationship has help.summary.}
  - {id: DICT-008, severity: error, rule: ui.group, when stated, names a group in `groups.order`.}
  - {id: DICT-009, severity: error, rule: ui.recordLabel, when stated, names attributes the entity declares.}
  - {id: DICT-010, severity: error, rule: Every enumeration has a table (see enumeration-semantics.yaml), and its name does not collide with an entity.}
/specification/enumeration-semantics.yam:
# CEDM Enumeration Semantics
#
# An enumeration is a business concept in its own right, not a constraint on a
# column: its values are maintained by the business (reworded, ordered,
# retired, extended), they carry a meaning each, and other things refer to
# them. So every enumeration in CEDM has a **business table** in an application
# generated from it, exactly as every entity does — a window to maintain it, a
# row per value, an audit trail, access control.
#
# The attribute that uses an enumeration keeps storing the value (its `code`):
# lifecycles, rules and integrations compare it as text, and a status that
# changed from a string to a key would break every one of them. What changes is
# where the list comes from. The attribute's dropdown is fed from the table
# (the dictionary's Table reference: `sys_ref_table`), so a value added, reworded
# or retired in the table is what the form offers.
specification:
  name: CEDM Enumeration Semantics
  version: 1.0.0
  status: draft

enumeration:
  identity:
    name:
      rule: <Entity><Attribute> in PascalCase — SalesOrder.status is SalesOrderStatus.
      uniqueness: An enumeration name is unique among enumerations and among entities. DICT-010.
    owner: The entity and attribute that declare the values. Another attribute with the same values declares its own enumeration.
    registry: domain/enumerations/index.yaml — one entry per enumeration, generated from the entity files by tools/build_enumerations.py and checked in sync by tools/validate.py.

  declaration:
    where: An attribute of type enum states `values`.
    values:
      rule: Non-empty, unique, each a single token of upper-case words (SENT, PARTIALLY_FULFILLED) or the lower-case form a model already uses; stored and compared exactly as written.
    meanings: help.valueSemantics gives one sentence per value, keyed by the value. DICT-005.
    labels:
      optional: true
      key: help.valueLabels
      rule: One short label per value, where the label is not the value split into words.
    order: The order of `values` is the order of the dropdown and of the table's `sequence`.

  table:
    name: bus_<snake_case of the enumeration name>
    entityKind: reference_data
    window:
      name: The enumeration name split into words (Sales Order Status).
      category: Reference Data
      icon: list
    columns:
      - {name: id, type: uuid, key: true, generated: true}
      - {name: code, type: string, maxLength: 100, required: true, unique: true, immutable: true, help: The value stored in every column that uses this enumeration. Fixed once created, because lifecycles, rules and integrations compare it as text.}
      - {name: name, type: string, maxLength: 200, required: true, help: What a person reads in a dropdown and on a record. Reword freely; the code is unaffected.}
      - {name: description, type: text, required: false, help: What the value means to the business — the enumeration's help.valueSemantics entry for it.}
      - {name: sequence, type: integer, required: true, help: The position of the value in a dropdown, lowest first.}
      - {name: isActive, type: boolean, required: true, default: true, help: Whether the value is offered on new records. A retired value stays on the records that already carry it.}
    identifier: [name]
    rows:
      source: values, in order
      id: Deterministic (UUIDv5 over the enumeration name and the value), so seeding is idempotent and stable across regeneration.
      code: the value
      name: valueLabels[value], else the value split into words and capitalised
      description: valueSemantics[value]
      sequence: 10, 20, 30 … in declaration order
      isActive: true
    seeding: "The rows are application data, not sample data: they are written by the dictionary seed and never generated, randomised or skipped."
    access: Maintained by an administrator. Readable by anyone who can read an entity that uses the enumeration.

  dictionary:
    reference: One sys_reference per enumeration, validation type Table (T).
    ref_table:
      table: the enumeration's table
      key_column: code
      display_column: name
      order_by: sequence
      where: is_active = true
    attribute_column: sys_column.sys_reference_id is that reference; the column stays a string.
    ref_list: Not used. The table is the single source for the list, so there is no second copy to drift.

  integrity:
    - A record may carry a value whose row has since been retired; it keeps the value and the form shows it.
    - A value that is not in the table is refused on write, as it was when the list was fixed.
    - Deleting a row that a record carries is refused.

rules:
  - {id: ENUM-001, rule: Every enumerated attribute declares an enumeration, and every enumeration has a table.}
  - {id: ENUM-002, rule: The registry lists exactly the enumerations the entity files declare, with their values, in order.}
  - {id: ENUM-003, rule: An enumeration's table name collides with no entity's table.}
  - {id: ENUM-004, rule: help.valueSemantics has a key for every value and no other.}
  - {id: ENUM-005, rule: A value is stored exactly as the table's code holds it.}

/specification/help-semantics.yaml:
# CEDM Help and Semantic Documentation Contract
# Every entity and every field must carry human-readable semantic help.

helpContract:
  version: 1.0.0
  mandatory: true

entityHelp:
  required:
    - summary
    - purpose
    - businessMeaning
    - whenUsed
    - howItRelates
    - lifecycleUsage
    - commonProcesses
    - commonExamples
  fields:
    summary: One concise explanation of what the entity represents.
    purpose: Why the entity exists in a business application.
    businessMeaning: The real-world business concept represented by the entity.
    whenUsed: When users, processes, or systems create, read, update, or reference it.
    howItRelates: Explanation of how it connects to important related entities and why those relationships matter.
    lifecycleUsage: How the entity participates in lifecycle/state transitions and what those states mean operationally.
    commonProcesses: Business processes in which the entity is normally involved.
    commonExamples: Concrete examples of valid business situations represented by the entity.
    distinctions: Important distinctions from similarly named or related entities.
    synonyms: Business terms commonly used for the concept.
    uiGuidance: Guidance for forms, lists, search, object pages, dashboards, and user actions.

fieldHelp:
  required:
    - summary
    - businessMeaning
    - usage
    - relationshipContext
  fields:
    summary: Plain-language explanation of what the field stores.
    businessMeaning: What the value means to the business, not merely its technical type.
    usage: How the field is populated, read, validated, searched, filtered, calculated, or displayed.
    relationshipContext: How the field participates in the entity's relationships or connects the entity to other business concepts.
    valueSemantics: Meaning of allowed values, units, signs, precision, and nullability where applicable.
    lifecycleImpact: How the field affects or is affected by entity lifecycle states.
    examples: Representative valid values and business scenarios.
    validationGuidance: Business validation beyond primitive datatype constraints.
    uiGuidance: Recommended label, tooltip, help text, visibility, editability, and search behavior.
    securityGuidance: Whether the field is sensitive, restricted, or subject to masking.

referenceHelp:
  rule: Every reference field must explain both the target concept and why the relationship exists.
  requiredDetails:
    - targetMeaning
    - relationshipPurpose
    - cardinalityMeaning
    - navigationUse

enumHelp:
  rule: Every enumerated value must have a business explanation.
  valueFields:
    - code
    - label
    - meaning
    - usage

qualityRules:
  minimumEntitySummaryWords: 15
  minimumFieldSummaryWords: 8
  genericTextRejected:
    - "Stores the value."
    - "The field value."
    - "Identifier."
    - "Name of the entity."
    - "Used for reference."
  contextualRequirement: Help must describe the concept in its CEDM business context and must not merely restate the field name or datatype.

/specification/lifecycle.yaml:
specification:
  name: CEDM Lifecycle Semantics
  version: 0.1.0
  status: draft

lifecycle:
  principles:
    - Lifecycle state is domain data, not merely UI state.
    - Valid transitions must be explicitly declared where lifecycle is material.
    - Terminal states require explicit domain semantics.
    - Invalid transitions must be rejected before persistence.

  transition:
    requiredFields:
      - from
      - to
    optionalFields:
      - action
      - guard
      - sideEffects
      - authorization
      - auditEvent

  standardStateSets:
    masterData: [DRAFT, ACTIVE, INACTIVE, RETIRED]
    document: [DRAFT, ISSUED, APPROVED, CANCELLED, ARCHIVED]
    workflow: [DRAFT, ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, RETIRED]
    task: [CREATED, READY, ASSIGNED, IN_PROGRESS, BLOCKED, COMPLETED, CANCELLED, FAILED]
    transaction: [DRAFT, OPEN, APPROVED, POSTED, COMPLETED, CANCELLED, REVERSED]

  rules:
    - id: LIFE-001
      rule: A transition must originate from the entity's declared state set.
    - id: LIFE-002
      rule: A transition must terminate in the entity's declared state set.
    - id: LIFE-003
      rule: Terminal states must not have outgoing transitions unless explicitly marked reactivatable.
